summary: AngleSPICAKokkos::init_style() unconditionally copies the pair style's lj_type/lj1..lj4/rminsq/emin arrays, but the base class only sets those pointers when repflag is non-zero, so they are still nullptr and the loop dereferences null.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_spica_kokkos.cpp:379-390: 'int ntypes = atom->ntypes; for (int i = 1; i <= ntypes; i++) { for (int j = 1; j <= ntypes; j++) { k_lj_type.view_host()(i,j) = lj_type[i][j]; k_lj1.view_host()(i,j) = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(lj1[i][j]); ... k_emin.view_host()(i,j) = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(emin[i][j]); } }'. The base, src/CG-SPICA/angle_spica.cpp:294-321, does: 'repflag = 0; for (int i = 1; i <= atom->nangletypes; i++) if (repscale && (repscale[i] > 0.0)) repflag = 1; ... if (repflag) { lj1 = (double **) force->pair->extract("lj1",itmp); ... }' -- i.e. lj1..lj4, lj_type, rminsq and emin are only assigned inside 'if (repflag)'. They are initialised to nullptr in the AngleSPICA constructor (src/CG-SPICA/angle_spica.cpp:47-52). The kernel itself correctly guards its use with 'if (repflag)' (src/KOKKOS/angle_spica_kokkos.cpp:215), but init_style does not.
failure_scenario: Any input where the 1-3 repulsion is switched off for every angle type, e.g. 'angle_coeff * 50.0 173.0 0.0' (4-argument form sets repscale = 0.0, src/CG-SPICA/angle_spica.cpp:272) or the legacy 6-argument cg/cmm form with epsilon 0.0. repflag stays 0, lj_type is nullptr, and 'lj_type[1][1]' in init_style segfaults at the start of the run. The plain CPU angle_style spica runs this input fine.
suggested_fix: Wrap the ntypes x ntypes copy loop and the matching modify_host() calls in 'if (repflag) { ... }', mirroring the guard the base class and the device kernel already use.

summary: AngleSPICAKokkos's constructor never sets kokkosable = 1, so angle_style hybrid/kk rejects spica/kk and VerletKokkos turns on auto_sync (a full host/device round trip of x and f) every timestep.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_spica_kokkos.cpp:44-54 is the whole constructor: 'AngleSPICAKokkos<DeviceType>::AngleSPICAKokkos(LAMMPS *lmp) : AngleSPICA(lmp) { atomKK = (AtomKokkos *) atom; neighborKK = (NeighborKokkos *) neighbor; execution_space = ExecutionSpaceFromDevice<DeviceType>::space; datamask_read = X_MASK | F_MASK | TYPE_MASK | ENERGY_MASK | VIRIAL_MASK; datamask_modify = F_MASK | ENERGY_MASK | VIRIAL_MASK; centroidstressflag = CENTROID_NOTAVAIL; }' -- no 'kokkosable = 1;'. Every sibling sets it as the first statement: angle_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:41, angle_mm3_kokkos.cpp:41, angle_mwlc_kokkos.cpp:35, angle_quartic_kokkos.cpp:37, angle_table_kokkos.cpp:42, angle_hybrid_kokkos.cpp:35. Consumers: src/KOKKOS/angle_hybrid_kokkos.cpp:203-204 'if (!styles[m]->kokkosable) error->all(FLERR,"Must use only Kokkos-enabled angle styles with angle_style hybrid/kk");' and src/KOKKOS/verlet_kokkos.cpp:473-474 'int prev_auto_sync = lmp->kokkos->auto_sync; if (!force->angle->kokkosable) lmp->kokkos->auto_sync = 1;' (same at dynamical_matrix_kokkos.cpp:247). auto_sync = 1 makes AtomKokkos::sync/modified push everything through the legacy host arrays (src/KOKKOS/atom_kokkos.cpp:241-269).
failure_scenario: 'angle_style hybrid/kk spica harmonic' aborts with 'Must use only Kokkos-enabled angle styles with angle_style hybrid/kk' even though spica/kk is a full KOKKOS port. With a plain 'angle_style spica/kk' on a GPU, every step copies x and f device->host->device around the angle compute, so the /kk variant is far slower than intended.
suggested_fix: Add 'kokkosable = 1;' as the first statement of AngleSPICAKokkos's constructor, matching every other KOKKOS angle style.

summary: angle spica/kk destroys and re-creates the k_eatom/k_vatom dual views on every energy/virial-tally step instead of only when maxeatom/maxvatom grows.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_spica_kokkos.cpp:79-88: 'if (eflag_atom) { memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_eatom,eatom); memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_eatom,eatom,maxeatom,"angle:eatom"); d_eatom = k_eatom.template view<DeviceType>(); } if (vflag_atom) { memoryKK->destroy_kokkos(k_vatom,vatom); ... }', versus the guarded form in src/KOKKOS/angle_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:74-87 / angle_table_kokkos.cpp:75-88 / angle_mwlc_kokkos.cpp:66-79.
failure_scenario: Same as angle_mm3_kokkos.cpp:72 -- per-atom energy/stress output turns every tally step into two device allocations and frees.
suggested_fix: Adopt the extent-guarded reallocation plus Kokkos::deep_copy(...,0.0) used by the other angle kk styles.

summary: k_setflag/d_setflag and k_repscale/d_repscale are allocated, filled, synced and carried into the device functor but are never read by any kernel.
evidence: Allocated at src/KOKKOS/angle_spica_kokkos.cpp:335 and 334 ('k_repscale = DAT::tdual_kkfloat_1d("AngleSPICA::repscale",nangletypes+1); k_setflag = DAT::tdual_int_1d("AngleSPICA::setflag",nangletypes+1);'), filled in coeff() (lines 416-417) and read_restart() (lines 439-440), synced in compute() (line 92 'k_repscale.template sync<DeviceType>();'), and declared as members at src/KOKKOS/angle_spica_kokkos.h:92-96. Neither d_setflag nor d_repscale appears anywhere in operator(), ev_tally or ev_tally13 (the whole file contains no other occurrence). The base class likewise only uses repscale to derive repflag (src/CG-SPICA/angle_spica.cpp:300-301).
failure_scenario: No wrong results; it wastes device memory and one host->device transfer per step, and it misleads a reader into thinking the 1-3 repulsion is per-type scaled on the device when it is not.
suggested_fix: Delete k_setflag/d_setflag and k_repscale/d_repscale (and the sync at line 92), or use d_repscale in the kernel if per-type scaling of the 1-3 term is actually intended.

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly); found by group 01
summary: AngleSPICAKokkos::init_style() unconditionally copies lj_type/lj1..lj4/rminsq/emin from the pair style, but AngleSPICA::init_style() only sets those pointers when repflag != 0, so with 1-3 repulsion disabled they are nullptr and the copy loop crashes.
evidence: angle_spica_kokkos.cpp:379-390 unguarded loop; src/CG-SPICA/angle_spica.cpp:299-314 sets repflag and extracts lj1/lj_type only 'if (repflag)'.
failure_scenario: angle_coeff * K theta0 0.0 (repscale 0) with angle_style spica/kk -> segfault at run start; CPU style runs fine.
suggested_fix: Wrap the copy loop and modify_host() calls in if (repflag).

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly); found by group 01
summary: AngleSPICAKokkos constructor never sets kokkosable = 1, so hybrid/kk rejects it ('Must use only Kokkos-enabled angle styles') and VerletKokkos enables auto_sync (full host round trip of x/f every step) for a plain spica/kk run.
evidence: grep kokkosable angle_spica_kokkos.cpp: no hits; every sibling sets it (angle_harmonic_kokkos.cpp:41); verlet_kokkos.cpp:473-474 and angle_hybrid_kokkos.cpp:203.
failure_scenario: 'angle_style hybrid/kk spica harmonic' aborts; plain spica/kk runs at host speed on a GPU.
suggested_fix: Add kokkosable = 1; in the constructor.

summary: pair snap/kk never strips the special-bond bits from the neighbor index (`j &= NEIGHMASK` is missing), so in a molecular system it dereferences out-of-range atom indices.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_snap_kokkos_impl.h:554 `T_INT j = d_neighbors(i,jj);` then `x(j,0)`, `type(j)` (lines 555-559); again at 581 `T_INT j = d_neighbors(i,jj);` with `snaKK.inside(ii,offset) = j;` (line 591); and in the CPU path at 634 and 653. `grep -n NEIGHMASK src/KOKKOS/pair_snap_kokkos_impl.h` returns nothing, while the CPU base does mask: src/ML-SNAP/pair_snap.cpp:142-143 `j = jlist[jj]; j &= NEIGHMASK;` (also at 315-316), and sibling KOKKOS manybody styles do too (src/KOKKOS/pair_sw_kokkos.cpp:233-234, src/KOKKOS/pair_tersoff_kokkos.cpp:350-351). The KOKKOS neighbor build really does set those bits: src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.cpp:500 and :726 `neighbors_i(n++) = j ^ (which << SBBITS);` for `molecular != Atom::ATOMIC`.
failure_scenario: A molecular system (atom_style full/molecular) where Neighbor::init sets special_flag=2 - which src/neighbor.cpp:557-558 does for EVERY special weight as soon as a kspace_style is defined - run with `pair_style hybrid/overlay snap/kk ... coul/long/kk` : neighbor entries for 1-2/1-3/1-4 pairs carry the SBBITS, so snap/kk reads x/type at index j|(which<<30), i.e. far past the end of the per-atom views -> garbage rij/type, wrong forces or a segfault; the stored `snaKK.inside` index is then used for `a_f(j,*) -= fij[*]` (line 1382) writing out of bounds.
suggested_fix: Add `j &= NEIGHMASK;` immediately after every `d_neighbors(i,jj)` read in TagPairSNAPComputeNeigh and TagPairSNAPComputeNeighCPU (lines 554, 581, 634, 653).

summary: TagPairSNAPPreUi looks up the atom type with the chunk-relative index instead of the real atom index, so with chunking (inum > chunksize) it initializes ulisttot with the wrong element for chem-SNAP potentials.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_snap_kokkos_impl.h:711-718 `const int iatom = iatom_mod + iatom_div * vector_length; if (iatom >= chunk_size) return; int itype = type(iatom); int ielem = d_map[itype]; snaKK.pre_ui(iatom, j, ielem);` (same in the two other PreUi overloads, lines 724-731 and 736-744). Every other kernel in the same file converts first: e.g. line 534 `const int i = d_ilist[ii + chunk_offset];`, lines 986-988, 999-1001, 1012-1014, 1035-1037, 1048-1050, 1061-1063, 1365. `chunk_offset` is advanced by `chunk_offset += chunk_size;` (line 388) inside the chunking loop (line 191), and the KOKKOS neighbor build sets `d_ilist(i) = i` (src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.cpp:593 etc.), so `type(iatom)` is the type of atom `iatom` rather than of atom `iatom + chunk_offset`. `ielem` selects the diagonal element block in SNAKokkos::pre_ui (src/KOKKOS/sna_kokkos_impl.h: `if (ma == mb && (!chem_flag || ielem == jelem || wselfall_flag)) { re_part = wself; }`).
failure_scenario: A chemflag SNAP potential (`chemflag 1`, wselfall off) with more than `chunksize` (default 32768, src/ML-SNAP/pair_snap.cpp:636) local atoms per MPI rank: for every chunk after the first, `wself` is placed in the element block of the wrong atom, giving wrong bispectrum components, energies and forces. Silent - results simply differ from pair_style snap and from a smaller-chunksize run.
suggested_fix: In all three TagPairSNAPPreUi overloads, replace `type(iatom)` with `type(d_ilist[iatom + chunk_offset])`, matching TagPairSNAPComputeBetaLinear.

summary: The neighbor screening drops the CPU base's `rsq > 1e-20` guard, so a neighbor exactly on top of atom i enters the SNAP kernels with r == 0.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_snap_kokkos_impl.h:562 `if (rsq >= rnd_cutsq(itype,jtype)) { jtype = -1; }` and line 642/662 `if (rsq < rnd_cutsq(itype,jtype))`, versus src/ML-SNAP/pair_snap.cpp:151 `if (rsq < cutsq[itype][jtype]&&rsq>1e-20) {`. The same guard is present in every CPU ML-SNAP style (compute_sna_atom.cpp:417, compute_snad_atom.cpp:318, compute_snap.cpp:400, compute_snav_atom.cpp:314, pair_snap.cpp:324).
failure_scenario: Two coincident atoms (or a self-image in a box smaller than the cutoff) yield r = 0; the CPU style skips the pair, snap/kk divides by zero in compute_cayley_klein / compute_ui and produces NaN forces for the whole configuration.
suggested_fix: Add the `&& rsq > 1e-20` condition to the cutoff test in both TagPairSNAPComputeNeigh and TagPairSNAPComputeNeighCPU.

summary: pair snap/kk never strips the special-bond bits from a neighbour index: there is no 'j &= NEIGHMASK' anywhere in the file. In a molecular system whose neighbour entries carry SBBITS the style reads x/type far past the end of the per-atom views and later writes forces at the same bogus index.
verified_by: orchestrator (grep NEIGHMASK over src/KOKKOS/pair_snap_kokkos_impl.h returns nothing; the read is at :554 and :581. The CPU base masks at src/ML-SNAP/pair_snap.cpp:143, and the sibling KOKKOS manybody style does too at src/KOKKOS/pair_sw_kokkos.cpp:234. The bits really are set: src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.cpp:500 stores 'j ^ (which << SBBITS)', and src/neighbor.cpp:557-558 forces special_flag[1..3]=2 whenever a kspace style is defined.)

summary: NPairTrimKokkos's constructor never sets execution_space, so it keeps the NPair default of Host and the device build syncs x to the host instead of the device.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_trim_kokkos.cpp:27 'NPairTrimKokkos<DeviceType>::NPairTrimKokkos(LAMMPS *lmp) : NPair(lmp) {}' - no 'execution_space = ExecutionSpaceFromDevice<DeviceType>::space;'.  The base sets 'execution_space = Host;' in src/npair.cpp:44.  The sibling styles do set it: src/KOKKOS/npair_halffull_kokkos.cpp:33 and src/KOKKOS/npair_skip_kokkos.cpp:28.  It is then used in src/KOKKOS/npair_trim_kokkos.cpp:57 'atomKK->sync(execution_space,X_MASK);' immediately before the device kernel that reads 'x = atomKK->k_x.view<DeviceType>()' (:56, kernel at :94-111).
failure_scenario: With trim/kk/device, whenever x was last modified on the host (host-side comm/exchange/borders, a non-Kokkos fix touching x, read_restart) the device copy of x is never refreshed; the trim kernel computes rsq from stale coordinates and keeps/drops the wrong neighbors, giving wrong forces without any error.  It also forces a pointless device->host copy of x on every build.
suggested_fix: Set 'execution_space = ExecutionSpaceFromDevice<DeviceType>::space;' in the NPairTrimKokkos constructor.

summary: The trim test uses cutsq_custom unconditionally, dropping the CPU fallback to cutneighsq[itype][jtype] when the trimmed list's own request carries no custom cutoff.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_trim_kokkos.cpp:113 'if (rsq > cutsq_custom) continue;' and :179 (CPU path) with cutsq_custom = cutoff_custom*cutoff_custom (:38,:59).  The base src/npair_trim.cpp:89-90 does 'double cutsq_trim = (cutsq_custom > 0.0) ? cutsq_custom : cutneighsq[itype][jtype]; if (rsq > cutsq_trim) continue;'.  cutoff_custom is 0 unless the request set NeighRequest::cut (src/npair.cpp:96), while Neighbor::morph_copy_trim() sets trim=1 from 'icut != jcut' alone (src/neighbor.cpp:1576-1584), where a request without ->cut uses icut = cutneighmax.
failure_scenario: A list with the default cutoff that gets trimmed from a longer-cutoff parent list (parent requested a cutoff larger than cutneighmax) has cutoff_custom == 0, so cutsq_custom == 0 and 'rsq > 0.0' rejects every neighbor -> empty neighbor lists and zero forces, silently.
suggested_fix: Mirror the CPU fallback by passing the per-type cutneighsq into the functor as a device view and using it when cutsq_custom == 0, or refuse to build with an explicit error when TRIM and cutoff_custom == 0.

summary: trim_to_cpu reads atom->x (the host mirror) without syncing X_MASK to the host, so coordinates can be stale when the parent Kokkos list was built on the device.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_trim_kokkos.cpp:130-132 'listcopy_kk->k_ilist.sync_host(); double** x = atom->x;' - k_ilist is synced but nothing calls atomKK->sync(Host,X_MASK), while the distances at :174-177 are computed from that host x.  Compare trim_to_kokkos at :56-57 which does sync x (albeit to the wrong space, see the execution_space finding).
failure_scenario: A non-Kokkos style requesting a trimmed copy of a device-built Kokkos list (kk2cpu + trim) gets its neighbor pairs filtered with host coordinates from the previous device->host sync, so pairs are wrongly kept or dropped after any device-side integration step.
suggested_fix: Call 'atomKK->sync(Host,X_MASK);' at the top of NPairTrimKokkos::trim_to_cpu() before taking atom->x.

summary: The guard that decides whether to call group->inertia_extended() omits finite-size spheres, so the spin moment of inertia of atom_style sphere particles is silently dropped by compute inertia/kk.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_inertia_kokkos.cpp:96-107 comments 'the extended-particle contribution reads the ellipsoid, line, tri and body bonus arrays ... when none of those atom styles is present it adds nothing' and guards with 'if (atom->style_match("ellipsoid") || atom->style_match("line") || atom->style_match("tri") || atom->style_match("body")) { ... group->inertia_extended(igroup,itensor); }'. But Group::inertia_extended -> add_extended_inertia (src/group.cpp:1694-1725) has a sphere fallback that needs none of those atom vecs: ':1721-1722  } else if (radius && radius[i] > 0.0) { ivec[0] = ivec[1] = ivec[2] = SINERTIA * massone * radius[i] * radius[i]; }'. The CPU style calls it unconditionally: src/compute_inertia.cpp:63 'group->inertia_extended(igroup, itensor);'.
failure_scenario: 'atom_style sphere' granular run with 'compute I all inertia/kk': the three diagonal components are short by sum(0.4*m_i*r_i^2) compared to the non-KOKKOS 'compute inertia' on the same configuration.
suggested_fix: Add '|| atom->radius' (or atom->radius_flag) to the condition, or simply always call group->inertia_extended() after syncing the needed host arrays.

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly; found by group 04, line corrected)
summary: compute inertia/kk calls group->inertia_extended() only when an ellipsoid/line/tri/body atom style is present, but Group::add_extended_inertia also adds the 0.4*m*r^2 spin term for finite-size spheres (radius > 0), so for atom_style sphere the extended contribution is silently dropped.
evidence: compute_inertia_kokkos.cpp:56-62 guard; src/group.cpp:1722-1723 'else if (radius && radius[i] > 0.0) ivec[0..2] = SINERTIA*massone*radius[i]*radius[i]'; src/compute_inertia.cpp calls inertia_extended unconditionally.
failure_scenario: Granular (atom_style sphere) run with compute inertia/kk: diagonal components short by the sum of 0.4*m_i*r_i^2 compared with compute inertia.
suggested_fix: Extend the guard with atom->radius_flag (or always call inertia_extended after syncing the needed host arrays).

summary: TRIM branch uses cutsq_custom unconditionally and drops the CPU fallback to cutneighsq[itype][jtype], so a trim list whose own request has no custom cutoff (cutoff_custom==0) trims away every neighbor.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_halffull_kokkos.cpp:55 'cutsq_custom = cutoff_custom*cutoff_custom;' and :138/:150 'if (rsq > cutsq_custom) continue;'.  The CPU base src/npair_halffull.cpp:127-128 and :140-141 instead do 'double cutsq_trim = (cutsq_custom > 0.0) ? cutsq_custom : cutneighsq[itype][jtype]; if (rsq > cutsq_trim) continue;'.  The same fallback exists in src/npair_trim.cpp:89 and src/npair_skip.cpp:108.  cutoff_custom is only nonzero when the request set NeighRequest::cut (src/npair.cpp:96), yet Neighbor::morph_halffull()/morph_copy_trim() set trim=1 purely from 'icut != jcut' (src/neighbor.cpp:1495-1501, 1576-1584) where a request without ->cut gets icut = cutneighmax; a parent list requested with a cutoff LARGER than cutneighmax therefore produces a trimmed child whose own cutoff_custom is 0.
failure_scenario: A fix/compute requests a neighbor list with a cutoff larger than the pair-style cutoff+skin (e.g. fix nonaffine/displacement style requests), so the default-cutoff pair list becomes a halffull/trim child of it with cutoff_custom==0.  On CPU it is trimmed back to cutneighsq[itype][jtype]; with KOKKOS cutsq_custom==0 makes 'rsq > 0.0' true for every pair, so every half list is emptied and all pair forces/energies silently become zero.
suggested_fix: Mirror the CPU logic: pass the per-type cutneighsq (as a device dual view) into the functor and use 'const double cutsq_trim = (cutsq_custom > 0.0) ? cutsq_custom : d_cutneighsq(itype,jtype);' , or at minimum error out at build time when TRIM is set and cutoff_custom == 0.

summary: For NEWTON builds the ghost atoms of the parent full list are looped over and list->gnum is set from the parent, whereas the CPU base restricts both to the newtoff case.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_halffull_kokkos.cpp:61-62 'int inum_full = list->listfull->inum; if (list->ghost) inum_full += list->listfull->gnum;' and :79-80 'list->inum = k_list_full->inum; list->gnum = k_list_full->gnum;'.  src/npair_halffull.cpp:72-73 guards the same addition with 'if (!NEWTON)' and :155-157 sets 'list->inum = inum; if (!NEWTON) if (list->ghost) list->gnum = list->listfull->gnum;'.  The CPU header src/npair_halffull.h registers no NP_NEWTON|NP_GHOST halffull style at all, while npair_halffull_kokkos.h:101-149 does.
failure_scenario: A half+ghost neighbor list with newton on built by KOKKOS (halffull/newton/ghost/kk/*) fills half-list entries for ghost i atoms using the newton 'above and to the right' tie-break, which double counts (owner of the ghost stores the same pair) and reports gnum != 0 to consumers that assume newton ghost lists are empty.
suggested_fix: Either guard the ghost extension and gnum assignment with '!NEWTON' as the CPU version does, or remove the NP_NEWTON|NP_GHOST halffull KOKKOS style registrations if that combination is not supported.

summary: AtomNeighbors for the destination half list is constructed with d_numneigh(i), which is the not-yet-written (stale/uninitialized) half-list neighbor count.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/npair_halffull_kokkos.cpp:107-108 'const AtomNeighbors neighbors_i = AtomNeighbors(&d_neighbors(i,0),d_numneigh(i), &d_neighbors(i,1)-&d_neighbors(i,0));' - d_numneigh(i) is only assigned at :157 'd_numneigh(i) = n;', and d_numneigh is freshly allocated without initialization in src/KOKKOS/neigh_list_kokkos.cpp:46.
failure_scenario: Reads uninitialized device memory on the first build (harmless today because AtomNeighbors::num_neighs is never read here, but it trips memory checkers and would silently break if the member were ever used).
suggested_fix: Pass 0 (or the parent count d_numneigh_full(i)) instead of d_numneigh(i), or build the AtomNeighbors object after the count is known.

summary: FixShardlowKokkos binds the per-type mass array to a device view but never syncs atomKK->k_mass to the device, so on a GPU build the SSA kernel reads whatever the device copy of mass[] happens to contain.
evidence: fix_shardlow_kokkos.cpp:214-220 'if (atomKK->rmass) { massPerI = true; masses = atomKK->k_rmass.view<DeviceType>(); } else { massPerI = false; masses = atomKK->k_mass.view<DeviceType>(); }' - no 'atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>()' anywhere in the file ('grep -n k_mass src/KOKKOS/fix_shardlow_kokkos.cpp' returns only that line).  masses is then read inside the device kernel at fix_shardlow_kokkos.cpp:415 'const KK_FLOAT mass_i = masses(massPerI ? i : itype);' and :465 'const KK_FLOAT mass_j = masses(massPerI ? j : jtype);'.  There is no MASS bit in src/atom_masks.h (only RMASS_MASK, line 34), so the datamask sync at fix_shardlow_kokkos.cpp:619 'atomKK->sync(execution_space,X_MASK|V_MASK|TYPE_MASK|RMASS_MASK|UCOND_MASK|UMECH_MASK|DPDTHETA_MASK)' cannot cover it.  Every other KOKKOS style that reads k_mass on the device syncs it explicitly, e.g. src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46 'atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>();' and src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_kokkos.cpp:46,54.
failure_scenario: CUDA/HIP build, a dpd/fdt/energy system with per-type masses (no per-atom rmass) and a non-kk integrator (plain 'fix nve', which FixShardlow::setup accepts, src/DPD-REACT/fix_shardlow.cpp:158-165): nothing ever copies mass[] to the device, so massinv_i/massinv_j in ssa_update_dpde are computed from uninitialized device memory and the Shardlow velocity/energy updates are garbage or NaN.
suggested_fix: Add 'atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>();' in FixShardlowKokkos::init() (or right before the assignment in pre_neighbor()), matching fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46.

summary: fix shardlow/kk binds its `masses` device view to atomKK->k_mass without syncing the DualView to the device.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_shardlow_kokkos.cpp:214-219 `if (atomKK->rmass) { massPerI = true; masses = atomKK->k_rmass.view<DeviceType>(); } else { ... masses = atomKK->k_mass.view<DeviceType>(); }`, used at lines 270, 314, 415, 465 (`const double mass_i = masses(massPerI ? i : itype);`).  The file syncs many other DualViews (k_pairDPDE->k_cutsq line 139, np_ssa->k_ssa_* lines 574-580, k_params line 616) and the per-atom masks (lines 619, 658), but never `atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>()`; there is no MASS_MASK in src/atom_masks.h.
failure_scenario: GPU DPD-E run with per-type masses where no other KOKKOS style synced k_mass: mass_i/mass_j are 0, so the SSA momentum/energy exchange divides by zero and produces NaN velocities and internal energies.
suggested_fix: Add `atomKK->k_mass.modify_host(); atomKK->k_mass.sync<DeviceType>();` (the idiom used by FixNVEKokkos::init(), src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_kokkos.cpp:45-46) before the device view is used.

summary: The table temperature bounds lo and hi are stored in INTEGER Kokkos views in all three table structs, so the double bounds read from the EOS table file are truncated toward zero; every table index and every clamp in energy_lookup/temperature_lookup is then computed from the wrong lower bound.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_eos_table_rx_kokkos.h:93,99,105 all declare `typename AT::t_int_1d lo,hi;` / `HAT::t_int_1d lo,hi;`, while the CPU struct is src/DPD-REACT/fix_eos_table_rx.h:44-51 `struct Table { int ninput; double lo, hi; ... }` with src/DPD-REACT/fix_eos_table_rx.cpp:108-109 `tb->lo = tb->rfile[0]; tb->hi = tb->rfile[tb->ninput-1];` -- the first and last TEMPERATURE in the table file. The truncation happens at src/KOKKOS/fix_eos_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:563-564 `h_table->lo[i] = tb->lo; h_table->hi[i] = tb->hi;` (double -> int). The truncated value is then used for the index arithmetic at fix_eos_table_rx_kokkos.cpp:348-354 `thetai = MAX(thetai,d_table_const.lo(ispecies)); thetai = MIN(thetai,d_table_const.hi(ispecies)); itable = static_cast<int>((thetai - d_table_const.lo(ispecies)) * d_table_const.invdelta(ispecies));` whereas invdelta is still the correct double (fix_eos_table_rx.cpp:465-466 `tb->delta = (tb->hi - tb->lo)/tlm1`). That this is a copy-paste slip is visible in the parent it was cloned from: src/KOKKOS/pair_table_kokkos.h:71-92 has `t_int_1d nshiftbits,nmask;` in that slot and keeps the physical quantities as `t_double_1d innersq,invdelta,deltasq6;`.
failure_scenario: An EOS table whose first temperature is not an exact integer -- e.g. lo=0.5, hi=10.5, tablength=1000 so invdelta=99.9: lo is stored as 0 and hi as 10, thetai is clamped to [0,10] instead of [0.5,10.5], and for thetai=5.0 the code reads itable=499 instead of the correct 449, i.e. an energy from a completely different part of the table. At the top of the range itable reaches 999 while d_table_const.de only has tablength-1=999 entries (indices 0..998), so it also reads one element past the end of de. Every `fix eos/table/rx/kk` run with non-integer table bounds gets wrong internal energies/temperatures; the plain `fix eos/table/rx` gets them right.
suggested_fix: Change `lo,hi` to `typename AT::t_kkfloat_1d` / `HAT::t_kkfloat_1d` in all three structs (TableDeviceConst, TableDevice, TableHost) and cast with static_cast<KK_FLOAT> in create_kokkos_tables(), matching what pair_table_kokkos.h does for innersq/invdelta/deltasq6.

summary: PPPMKokkos does not override reset_grid(), so fix balance drives the inherited PPPM::reset_grid(), which dereferences the base-class gc (always nullptr for the KOKKOS style) and calls the non-virtual PPPM::compute_rho_coeff() on the never-allocated rho_coeff/drho_coeff pointers.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.h declares its own shadowing members 'Grid3dKokkos<DeviceType> *gc;' (:449) and a non-virtual 'void compute_rho_coeff();' (:486), while the base declares 'class Grid3d *gc;' (src/KSPACE/pppm.h:84) and the NON-virtual 'void compute_rho_coeff();' (src/KSPACE/pppm.h:142).  PPPMKokkos overrides neither reset_grid() nor allocates the base members, and src/KSPACE/pppm.cpp:637-668 'void PPPM::reset_grid() { deallocate(); ... allocate(); if (!overlap_allowed && !gc->ghost_adjacent()) ...; compute_gf_denom(); ... compute_rho_coeff(); setup(); }'.  The PPPM constructor leaves both at null ('fft1(nullptr), fft2(nullptr), remap(nullptr), gc(nullptr)' and 'rho1d = rho_coeff = drho1d = drho_coeff = nullptr;'), and PPPMKokkos::allocate() (src/KOKKOS/pppm_kokkos.cpp:791-892) only fills the KOKKOS members.  reset_grid() is invoked unconditionally by src/fix_balance.cpp:341 'if (force->kspace) force->kspace->reset_grid();'.
failure_scenario: 'kspace_style pppm/kk' together with 'fix balance ... ' (or any other caller of KSpace::reset_grid): on the first rebalance PPPM::reset_grid() evaluates gc->ghost_adjacent() on a null Grid3d* and then writes rho_coeff[l][m] through a null FFT_SCALAR** -> segmentation fault.
suggested_fix: Add a 'void reset_grid() override;' to PPPMKokkos that repeats the sequence using the KOKKOS members (and make PPPM::compute_rho_coeff() virtual so the KOKKOS version is picked up).

summary: Four setflag dual views are allocated as floating-point arrays, filled, and synced to the device on every compute() call, but no kernel ever reads them.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_class2_kokkos.cpp:100-103 syncs `k_setflag`, `k_setflag_a`, `k_setflag_bb`, `k_setflag_ba` each timestep; :339-342 allocates them as `DAT::tdual_kkfloat_1d` (integer flags stored as KK_FLOAT); :356-359 and :447-450 assign d_setflag/d_setflag_a/d_setflag_bb/d_setflag_ba; :386-389 and :465-468 fill them. The device views d_setflag* appear nowhere in operator() (:162-308) or ev_tally (:498-603), and the CPU base never reads setflag in compute() either (src/CLASS2/angle_class2.cpp:76-239).
failure_scenario: No wrong results; 4 extra device allocations of (nangletypes+1) KK_FLOATs plus 4 no-op DualView syncs per timestep, and integer flags stored in a float view (silently lossy above 2^24 - irrelevant for 0/1 but wrong typing).
suggested_fix: Delete k_setflag/k_setflag_a/k_setflag_bb/k_setflag_ba, their d_* views, and the corresponding allocate/coeff/read_restart/compute lines.

summary: `d_ba_r2 = k_ba_r2.template view<DeviceType>();` is duplicated in both allocate() and read_restart(), a copy-paste leftover that likely masks a missing assignment.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/angle_class2_kokkos.cpp:354-356: `d_ba_r1 = k_ba_r1.template view<DeviceType>();` / `d_ba_r2 = k_ba_r2.template view<DeviceType>();` / `d_ba_r2 = k_ba_r2.template view<DeviceType>();` and the identical pair at :445-446. All other d_* views are assigned exactly once.
failure_scenario: Harmless as written (the second assignment is idempotent), but it is the classic shape of a dropped `d_theta0`/`d_ba_k2` assignment and confuses future edits.
suggested_fix: Delete the duplicate line at 355 and at 446.

summary: The firstgroup loop-truncation is keyed on igroup but the shift kernel selects atoms with group2bit, so with 'atom_modify first <group>' plus the 'shift <other-group>' keyword the atoms of the shift group beyond nfirst are never displaced.
failure_scenario: atom_modify first mobile ; group mobile ... ; group shiftme ... ; fix 1 mobile recenter INIT INIT INIT shift shiftme  -> only the shiftme atoms that happen to sit in the first nfirst slots of the local atom list are recentered; the rest drift, and the /kk result differs from the non-kk result.
suggested_fix: Drop the firstgroup truncation (loop over atom->nlocal), or make it conditional on group2bit == groupbit.

summary: d_scale is copied to the device only inside coeff(), so later host-side changes to `scale` (fix adapt, and PairMEAM::init_one's symmetrization) never reach the device, and the lower triangle is copied from uninitialized memory.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/pair_meam_kokkos.cpp:296-310 is the only place d_scale is written; it runs from coeff(). src/MEAM/pair_meam.cpp:303-312 sets `scale[i][j] = 1.0` only for `j >= i`, and the j<i entries are first written in init_one (src/MEAM/pair_meam.cpp:353-354 `scale[j][i] = scale[i][j];`), which runs after coeff and is not overridden by PairMEAMKokkos - so the `for (int j = 1; j <= n; j++) h_scale(i,j) = scale[i][j];` loop reads memory->create'd but never-initialized doubles for j<i. `scale` is also exposed for run-time modification via PairMEAM::extract (src/MEAM/pair_meam.cpp:898 `if (strcmp(str,"scale")==0) return (void *) scale;`) and `fix adapt pair meam scale` is a documented feature (doc/src/fix_adapt.rst), but nothing re-uploads d_scale after fix adapt writes it.
failure_scenario: `fix adapt 1 pair meam scale 1 1 v_lambda` in a run with pair_style meam/kk: the host scale array changes every step but the device keeps the value captured at pair_coeff time, so the /kk run reproduces the unscaled potential while the CPU run scales it.
suggested_fix: Refresh d_scale from `scale` at the start of compute() (or in init_one/init_style), and initialize the whole scale array symmetrically before copying.

summary: Per-atom scratch arrays d_distsq/d_nearest/d_pairs are allocated as full inum x maxneigh / inum x npairs device arrays, so memory grows as O(natoms*maxneigh) where the CPU style uses a single maxneigh-sized buffer.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/compute_centro_atom_kokkos.cpp:121-126 'd_distsq = typename AT::t_kkfloat_2d("centro/atom:distsq",inum,maxneigh_kk); d_nearest = ...(inum,maxneigh_kk); d_pairs = ...(inum,npairs)' vs src/compute_centro_atom.cpp:179-180 'memory->create(distsq, maxneigh, ...)' (one row total) and :155 'auto *pairs = new double[npairs];'
failure_scenario: 1e7 local atoms with maxneigh~200 requires ~2e9 KK_FLOAT + 2e9 int of extra device memory (>16 GB) and aborts with a Kokkos allocation failure, while the CPU style needs only a few kB.
suggested_fix: Use per-thread scratch (team scratch memory or a bounded chunked RangePolicy over batches of atoms) instead of a full inum-by-maxneigh global scratch array.

summary: Three device-callable functions use unqualified sqrt()/cos()/sin() instead of the Kokkos:: math functions the rest of the file (and the KOKKOS package rules) use.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/math_extra_kokkos.h:526 (qnormalize) 'double norm = 1.0 / sqrt(q[0] * q[0] + ...);'; :722,:727,:732,:737 (exyz_to_q) 'q[0] = sqrt(q0sq);' etc.; :824-825 (no_squish_rotate) 'c_phi = cos(static_cast<double>(dt) * phi); s_phi = sin(static_cast<double>(dt) * phi);'. Every other function in the same header uses the qualified form, e.g. :108 'Kokkos::sqrt(v[0]*v[0]+...)', :207, :571-572 'Kokkos::sin(halfa) / Kokkos::cos(halfa)'. .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md rule 4: 'Use Kokkos:: math functions in device kernels (Kokkos::sqrt, Kokkos::exp, Kokkos::pow, Kokkos::log, ...), never std::'. All three are reached from device kernels: src/KOKKOS/fix_rigid_small_kokkos.cpp:854 'MathExtraKokkos::richardson(...)' (which calls qnormalize) and :1476 'MathExtraKokkos::qnormalize(quatatom);', src/KOKKOS/fix_rigid_nh_small_kokkos.cpp:665-669 'MathExtraKokkos::no_squish_rotate(...)'.
failure_scenario: Compiles today because CUDA/HIP inject ::sqrt/::cos/::sin device overloads for double via math.h, but the same construct is what rule 4 was written for; a backend that does not (or a KK_FLOAT=float build, where the unqualified call silently promotes to double) either fails to compile or costs double-precision transcendentals in a single-precision kernel.
suggested_fix: Replace with Kokkos::sqrt / Kokkos::cos / Kokkos::sin like the rest of the header.

summary: compute_forces() unconditionally marks the pair style's per-atom virial dual view host-modified and copies it to the device every step, even when per-atom virial tallying is off.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_descriptor_so3_kokkos.cpp:88-91 'auto d_vatom = data->k_pairmliap->k_vatom.template view<DeviceType>(); Kokkos::View<double[6], DeviceType> virial("virial"); data->k_pairmliap->k_vatom.modify_host(); data->k_pairmliap->k_vatom.template sync<DeviceType>();' -- neither statement is guarded by vflag_atom, unlike the matching write-back at lines 132-135 'if (vflag_atom) { ... modify<DeviceType>(); ... sync_host(); }'. The pair style has already put a zeroed k_vatom on both sides just before (src/KOKKOS/pair_mliap_kokkos.cpp:99-108), so the extra host->device copy is redundant even when vflag_atom is set.
failure_scenario: Every timestep copies the whole nmax x 6 vatom array host->device for nothing; on a GPU run without per-atom virial output this is a pure PCIe cost proportional to the atom count.
suggested_fix: Wrap the modify_host()/sync<DeviceType>() pair in 'if (vflag_atom)', or drop it entirely since pair_mliap_kokkos.cpp already leaves both sides zeroed and current.

summary: The Accelerator Variants line for pair_style pedone lists the variants out of alphabetical order (*pedone/omp* before *pedone/kk*).
evidence: doc/src/pair_pedone.rst:8 'Accelerator Variants: *pedone/omp*, *pedone/kk*'. .github/instructions/kokkos.instructions.md documentation checklist item 3 requires 'Add *<name>/kk* to the Accelerator Variants: line, ordered alphabetically'; doc/src/pair_nm.rst:17,22,27,32 do it correctly ('*nm/cut/kk*, *nm/cut/omp*').
failure_scenario: No runtime effect; inconsistent documentation ordering relative to every other accelerated style.
suggested_fix: Swap to 'Accelerator Variants: *pedone/kk*, *pedone/omp*'.
